evidence.AC_2: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. Evidence: test/letflow/engine/q1048_meridian_loan_ops_lead_escalation_test.exs lines 110-141. U holds role-credit-director (line 116) and role-loan-ops-lead (line 117). U completes l2-approval (line 120, 200). The disburse-loan escalation timer fires through the real Scheduler path (A.fire_escalation!, line 124; node_id asserted as disburse-loan at line 125; current node is the escalation at line 126). U's completion is refused (line 130): status 403, content type application/problem+json, and conn.resp_body equals the exact body {"detail":"separation of duties","status":403} (assert_separation!, lines 92-97). Instance rows (projection, tokens, tasks, event count, timers) are unchanged (line 131), and the escalation task stays pending (line 132). V also holds role-loan-ops-lead (line 117) and completes (line 134, 200). Task completed (line 135), projection completed (line 139), and no disbursement-held-notice dispatched (line 140). Leakage: the body is a constant, so no node id, user id or name can appear. FINDING (non-blocking): the test does not name end-disbursed. It infers the terminal node from status completed plus the absence of the held notice. The QA graph makes that inference sound (end-disbursed has exactly two incoming edges, e27 and e27-escalated, and the escalation's only completion edge is e27-escalated), but the assertion is not literal. test/support/req462_adoption.ex dispatched_nodes/2 reads service-task dispatch rows only, so it cannot prove an end node.
evidence.AC_5: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. Evidence: test/letflow/engine/q1048_meridian_loan_ops_lead_escalation_test.exs lines 299-336 and the helper assert_held_never_disbursed! (lines 288-297). Test 1: the only holder of role-loan-ops-lead is the refused completer u. u is refused with the separation body and the rows are unchanged (lines 313-315). The escalation timer then fires: escalation task cancelled (line 291), current node disbursement-held-notice (line 292), notice advanced, projection completed (lines 294-295), disbursement-held-notice dispatched (line 296). Test 2: no user holds role-loan-ops-lead; the same chain runs. Graph, parsed from test/fixtures/qa/meridian_loan_origination_process_definition.json: the escalation's timeout edge goes to disbursement-held-notice, whose single outgoing edge e41 goes to end-disbursement-held. end-disbursed has exactly two incoming edges: e27 (from disburse-loan) and e27-escalated (from the escalation). Each requires a holder of the node's role (ROLE check in lib/letflow/tasks.ex apply_completion_authz, around lines 585-590, against group membership resolved per request in resolve_principal_scope, around lines 362-374) and a separation-of-duties pass (separation_of_duties.ex check/5, under row locks). No route can force a node: POST /instances/:id/advance-timer (lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex line 356) fires only an armed timer, and its target comes from the Timer record. The claim-time separation check is fail-open and advisory, but completion re-checks under the locks, so it is not a bypass. No path reaches end-disbursed without a distinct eligible completer. FINDING (non-blocking): the test asserts held-notice dispatch and completed status but does not name end-disbursement-held or refute end-disbursed explicitly. A regression that reached end-disbursed would fail the held-notice assertion, so the property is pinned indirectly. Explicit assertions are recommended.
evidence.AC_6: PASS_WITH_FINDINGS. (a) Runtime meaning, from the code: escalation_role grants no eligibility. Readers in lib/ are exactly two: lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex around lines 1072-1122 (CHK-21, presence and pairing validation only) and lib/letflow/definitions/role_binding.ex lines 28-37 (task_roles/1, which feeds advisory unbound_task_role warnings through validation_warnings.ex and definitions.ex around line 1261; it never writes a binding and never grants). The engine, task activation and eligibility do not read it: the escalation task's assignee_ref is the node's own attributes["role"] (lib/letflow/engine/task_activation.ex around lines 130-141), and completion compares that value with the caller's DB-resolved role names (lib/letflow/tasks.ex around lines 585-590). Expected answer confirmed: no. (b) The attribute agrees with the routing: disburse-loan escalation_role is role-loan-ops-lead (QA JSON line 393; simulation yaml line 146); escalate-disburse-loan-to-loan-ops-lead role and escalation_role are role-loan-ops-lead (QA lines 435 and 437; simulation lines 158 and 160). The escalation node's distinct_from is exactly the six ids l1-approval, l2-approval, escalate-l2-approval-to-ceo, committee-vote-cro, committee-vote-director and committee-vote-ceo, and all six exist in the graph. (c) No approval node routes to role-loan-ops-lead: in the parsed QA JSON, the only nodes whose attributes name it are disburse-loan (escalation_role) and the escalation node. The simulation yaml agrees. (d) Roster: test/fixtures/uat/actors.yaml hannah entry (lines 67-71) is TASK_WORKER builtin with routing_roles [role-loan-ops-lead] and no approval role. scripts/seed_meridian_persona_actors.sh ROLES (line 39) includes role-loan-ops-lead, and PERSONAS (line 54) has actor-meridian-hannah|role-loan-ops-lead. The persona holds no approval role. FINDINGS (MINOR): the edge id timeout-escalate-disburse-loan-to-credit-director is kept in the QA JSON and in the simulation yaml (line 400), so the payment-release step still carries the credit-director id that the Q-1044 decision named a lasting trap. Also, lib/letflow/design/q915-regulatory-review-21day-timer-path.md line 19 says escalation_role has no reader in lib/; role_binding.ex has read it since REQ-455 check 4, so that design note is stale (documentation only).

issues.description: AC 2 test precision: test/letflow/engine/q1048_meridian_loan_ops_lead_escalation_test.exs (small-loan test) infers end-disbursed from status completed and the absence of the held notice. Add an explicit assertion on the terminal node (for example, the completed token or event at end-disbursed).
AC 5 test precision: the fail-closed tests (assert_held_never_disbursed!) do not name end-disbursement-held and do not refute end-disbursed. Add both explicit assertions.

Naming trap left behind: the edge id timeout-escalate-disburse-loan-to-credit-director still names credit-director on a payment-release step in test/fixtures/qa/meridian_loan_origination_process_definition.json and test/fixtures/simulation/meridian/process_claim_intake.yaml (line 400). The Q-1044 decision asked that the id not carry the old role. Rename in a follow-up that updates every reference, or in this PR if the rename is contained.

BA scope question, not an AC 5 failure. distinct_from covers only the six approval nodes. Assessment and decision nodes that set credit_decision, risk_rating or kyc_outcome are not named: credit-memo-review (role-credit-manager), risk-assessment (role-risk-manager), kyc-manual-review (role-compliance-officer), credit-memo-escalation-review (role-credit-director) and risk-assessment-escalation-review (role-cro). A holder of role-loan-ops-lead who completed one of them could release the payment through the escalation. disburse-loan has the same residual. Route to letflow-2 (BA) for a ruling.

Transitional rollout gap. Completion reads the instance snapshot (separation_of_duties.ex load_snapshot reads InstanceDefinitionSnapshot). Loans started on v1.14 keep the credit-director escalation and the L2 self-release residual until they end. The decision says QA only and no real payments. ORCH or the BA should drain in-flight v1.14 instances or record an acceptance.

Simulation copy parity. The simulation disburse-loan node has no distinct_from, and origin/main's simulation yaml has none on any node (a v1.1 port that predates REQ-465). This branch added distinct_from only to the escalation node, which matches the QA definition. The REQ-467 record defers the full resync to Q-1049 / GH #2391. Not introduced by this branch.
